newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end flat, underperform after election.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end flat, underperform after election.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed on Tuesday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, as investors responded to the narrow victory by the ruling Liberals in yesterday's federal election.

"People like the status quo, and if we're going to get a deviation from that then it's a devil that they don't know," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst for financial analysis firm Technical Data.
Canada's 30-year benchmark traded unchanged at C$112.47 to yield 6.999 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond firmed 11/32 to yield 6.87 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 13 basis points from 10 basis points at Monday's close.

"It was one of those buy the rumor, sell the news type situations. The market rallied into the election expecting a majority and when the majority came there was no more good news. Everything was fully priced in," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
The governing Liberals won 155 of the 301 seats in Canada's Parliament in yesterday's elections, a majority of just four seats.

Although bond prices firmed slightly on news of the majority, the narrow margin of the win provided little reason for the market to follow through on the intial gains, analysts said. As a result Canadian bonds traded weaker to little changed even as U.S. Treasuries rose on positive economic data there.

Both Canadian and U.S. bond investors are now looking ahead to the release of key employment data in both countries on Friday. Dealers said activity in the Canadian market was light during today's session, especially considering it followed a federal election.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.11 to C$105.54 to yield 6.487 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 9/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 18 basis points at the close on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.95 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.07 percent.
